structures: "How Burger King Lost to Wendy’s": McDonald's dominance and the fight for second → John Chidsey era: barbell, value and broilers → Wendy's overtakes; 3G buys Burger King → Daniel Schwartz: franchisor model and balance → Jose Sill: discounting and reclaim the flame → Analysis: pricing not product, peanut butter approach → Wendy's rise through values and product

"How Casper Failed & Why DTC Startups Lose Money": Casper everywhere online → The D2C model and investor hype → Unicorn valuation, Target offer → Embarrassing IPO and collapse → The numbers: losses and ad spend → Slow growth and slow mattress cycle → Retail becomes the growth channel → Europe shut down, bleak outlook

"How Dollar Tree Conquered Low Income America": Bigger is better, inflation hits → Dollar Tree's conquest of low-income America → What Dollar Tree is: products and store count → Small stores and treasure hunt → Family Dollar → Sales and margins versus Target and Walmart → Expansion: mammoths versus hare

"The Dreadful Business of Balding & Hair Loss": Balding facts and narrator's story → Three options: nothing, shave, fight back → Prosthesis: wigs and toupees → Medication: finasteride and Merck → Minoxidil → Hair transplant surgery → Choosing Korea and Dr. Kim → The surgery and cost

"Tree to Box: The Billion Dollar Cardboard Business": The world runs on cardboard → Types of cardboard and how it's made → Forests, fiber and supply chain → Local business and vertical integration → Name of the game is volume → International Paper's streamlining → International Paper's pedestrian results → Westrock's innovation strategy → Comparison and hidden empires

"Why Football Is Bad Business": Football's success versus its finances → Premier League and Manchester United's flywheel → Player salaries erase the profit → Juventus and the Ronaldo bet → Barcelona on the edge of collapse → Super League and billionaire owners

"Why Starbucks Must Crush Unions to Survive": Starbucks' image: CSR montage and Schultz clips → The irony of Starbucks versus its unions → Three waves of coffee and beverage economics → Howard Schultz and why he can crush unions → Post-2000 decline and Schultz's 2008 return → Licensing model and the 2008 to 2017 boom → China, Europe and Schultz's exit in 2017 → Schultz returns in 2022; union cost math → Pressure on margins and conclusion

Variety: the channel's films differ — e.g. text share varies by 24% across films; two films' looks differ by 0.14 (within one film 0.022). Land each film somewhere different inside the band, not on the average.

Grade: the look moves between chapters — saturation shifts by about 0.126 and brightness by 0.117 (0–1 scale) between a film's chapters; across the film saturation runs 0.301 → 0.284 → 0.28 → 0.304 → 0.29 → 0.28 → 0.284 → 0.306 → 0.291 → 0.28.
